_why: ADR 0097's mutation table, re-derived under scripts/mutate.py.
ADR 0093 found the clone URL stated three ways and made README.md,
START_HERE.md and CONTRIBUTING.md agree. It picked `math12345678/caterva`
because that is what README happened to say, without counting how often
each spelling appeared. The count was 3 against 126 -- and the 126
included all five contact_links on .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml,
the GitHub New Issue page, which a newcomer reaches before cloning
anything.
So the repair reduced a three-way disagreement among three files and
left the repository more inconsistent than it found it, while reporting
the problem as fixed. The owner confirmed math12345678/caterva on
S1 and S2 are the widened check. A blob URL whose path resolves to a
file in this tree is a claim about THIS repository, whoever it says owns
it -- evidence rather than a name, so the planned split repos
(Terrium-sim/frontend-main and the rest) are correctly not caught.
C4 and C5 are the two things the new test-count matcher must NOT do.
docs/readmes/business.md records a real incident in which 275 tests
failed; docs/FIRST_TASKS.md cites 1,291 tests as the defect it warns
about. Rewriting either would falsify a record to make a build go green.
Run:  python3 scripts/mutate.py --set docs/mutations/adr-0097-agreement-among-the-files-i-was-reading.json

mutations.description: the agreement check narrows back to the three entry-point documents
mutations._note: The defect exactly. With SELF_REFERENCES back to ENTRY_POINTS, the New Issue page and docs/REPO_MAP.md leave the scope and can disagree freely.

mutations.description: a self-link is accepted without checking the path exists here
mutations._note: Dropping the existence test turns the rule from evidence into a name match, and the eighteen planned split repos start being demanded to agree with the monorepo -- a guard that fails on correct documents is a guard that gets deleted. Escaped on the first run: every blob URL in the real files happens to resolve, so the rule was invisible. extract_self_links() was split out to be testable on synthetic input.

mutations.description: clone_commands() reads only the entry points again
mutations._note:
This is how docs/REPO_MAP.md kept `git clone --recursive .../main.git` -- both halves of a defect that had been fixed two files away.
    Three false readings before a true one, all recorded because each was a different failure. (1) INDETERMINATE: the find string matched both clone_commands() and self_links(), whose opening lines are identical. (2) NOT CAUGHT, correctly: once REPO_MAP was fixed there was nothing left for the wider scope to catch, so the scope could be reverted and the suite would agree -- coverage that exists only while a defect exists is not coverage. test_the_scan_reaches_past_the_three_entry_points now asserts the scope directly. (3) NOT CAUGHT again, this time wrongly: that test took the union of clone_commands() and self_links(), so narrowing either alone was still satisfied by the other. Asserted separately now. (4) NOT CAUGHT a third time and unreproducible -- applying the identical edit by hand failed the test. It went away after `rm -rf Tests/__pycache__`. Stale bytecode is a false NOT CAUGHT that looks exactly like a real gap, which is the reason ADR 0069 exists.

mutations.description: the test-count matcher reads a report of tests failing as a suite size
mutations._note: docs/readmes/business.md: 'a guard that printed "every collected test ran" while 275 tests failed'. A count of tests that failed is not a count of tests, and correcting it would edit the record of the incident.

mutations.description: the test-count matcher stops honouring quotation
mutations._note: docs/FIRST_TASKS.md cites '22 guards and 1,291 tests' as the defect it is warning about. The project's existing convention -- plain means assert, quoted means cite -- is what keeps that sentence writable.

mutations.description: an uncollected suite makes every test count look stale
mutations._note: With no baseline, every claim differs from every real figure. Reporting the whole repository as wrong the moment pytest cannot run is a guard nobody will believe the second time.
mutations.find:
if not actual:
        return []  # nothing collected; see rewrite() on inventing numbers

mutations.description: the drafted public READMEs drop out of the checked set
mutations._note: They are the file GitHub renders first on every repository the split would create. Not-live-yet was the reason nothing checked them, and it is the reason they matter most.
